papers.title_en: BanglaKontho: Closing the Long-Form Gap in Bangla Text-to-Speech
papers.evidence: 孟加拉语TTS语料库构建与预处理管线
papers.tldr: 孟加拉语作为世界第七大语言，神经文本转语音资源严重不足，现有语料以短句为主，缺乏长形式韵律与一致叙述。我们发布 BanglaKontho，一个来自专业有声读物的 20 小时单说话者孟加拉 TTS 语料库，包含 7,050 条带转录话语，并配套文本规范化器与预处理管线。基于该语料从头训练的 MB-iSTFT-VITS 基线词错率 9.5%、自然度 MOS 4.46，显著优于在 12 小时 IndicTTS-Bn 上重训的 16.0% 和 3.16。该资源以 CC BY-NC 4.0 开放，为孟加拉长形式语音合成填补空白。
papers.abstract_en: Bangla, the seventh most spoken language in the world, remains under-resourced for neural text-to-speech. Public Bangla speech corpora are dominated by short read-prompt utterances collected for speech recognition, leaving long-form prosody and consistent single-speaker narration uncovered. We present BanglaKontho, a single-speaker Bangla TTS corpus of 20 hours derived from professional audiobook recordings: 7,050 segmented utterances with verified transcripts at 24 kHz. We also release a reusable Bangla text normalizer covering Bangladeshi-style digit grouping, currency and date expressions, Danda punctuation and Unicode normalization, together with the full preprocessing pipeline. An MB-iSTFT-VITS baseline trained from scratch reaches 9.5% WER and 4.46 naturalness MOS, against 16.0% and 3.16 for the same architecture retrained on the 12-hour IndicTTS-Bn corpus. The corpus is released openly under CC BY-NC 4.0.

papers.title_en: VietPrism: A large-scale Vietnamese speech and deepfake corpus with diverse dialects and code-switching
papers.evidence: 包含转写、说话人身份、方言和语码转换的大规模多领域语音语料库
papers.tldr: 越南语语音研究长期受资源孤岛限制，缺乏能同时覆盖方言、语码转换和深度伪造的大规模数据。VietPrism首次大规模整合这些维度，收集993.4小时真实语音、403,941条话语、五个方言组及近半时长的越英语码转换，并生成超3.1K小时受控欺骗语音。对五个多语言检测器的零样本评估发现，EER因检测器-生成器配对而大幅波动，DFA-1B随说话人相似度增加从16.3%升至33.6%，方言分层结果进一步揭示模型依赖差异。该语料库为越南语语音建模和可信音频深度伪造检测提供了挑战性基础。
papers.abstract_en: Vietnamese speech research is constrained by resources that isolate automatic speech recognition from speaker, dialect, code-switching, and deepfake analysis. We introduce VietPrism, an open, multi-domain corpus that brings these dimensions together at scale: 993.4 hours and 403,941 bona fide utterances from 1,262 verified speakers across 8,388 real-world videos. To our knowledge, it is the first large-scale Vietnamese corpus to jointly provide transcripts, consistent speaker identities, five dialect groups, and naturally occurring Vietnamese--English code-switching, which constitutes nearly half of the corpus by duration. We further create over 3.1K hours of spoof speech with four open-source and commercial synthesis systems. Every spoof is conditioned on a verified speaker reference and paired with a transcript- and speaker-matched bona fide utterance, enabling unique controlled evaluation with reduced lexical and identity confounds. Zero-shot evaluation of five pretrained multilingual detectors reveals striking brittleness: EER greatly varies across detector--generator pairings, while recent multilingual detector DFA-1B degrades from 16.3% to 33.6% as speaker similarity increases. Dialect-stratified results expose further model-dependent disparities. By unifying natural linguistic diversity with controlled spoof generation, VietPrism provides a challenging foundation for Vietnamese speech modeling and trustworthy audio-deepfake detection.

papers.title_en: MuLA-Bench: A Multilingual Long-Form Audio Understanding Benchmark via Multi-Tier Auditing
papers.authors: Zeyu Yang, Xinyu Zhang, Zibo Bi, Pei Zhang, Xize Cheng, Jin Xu, Baosong Yang, Satoshi Nakamura
papers.evidence: 多语言长格式音频理解基准及多级审计
papers.tldr: 现有长音频模型评估依赖上下文长度和总体准确率，掩盖了语言、证据与任务对难度的共同作用。MuLA-Bench提出多语言长音频理解基准，涵盖16种语言、8个领域、1769段实录、5038个开放式问题，采用语义与声学双轨道及证据审计。对十个音频语言模型的评估显示，语言排名跨领域任务变化、声学-语义性能差异显著、时间对齐易错。该基准暴露了单一长上下文分数无法捕捉的条件性失败模式。
papers.abstract_en: Long-form audio performance is often summarized by context length and aggregate accuracy, obscuring how language, evidence, and task jointly shape difficulty. We introduce MuLA-Bench: 5,038 open-ended questions over 1,769 in-the-wild recordings totaling 1,377.9 hours, covering 16 languages and eight domains. A balanced Language x Domain semantic track supports controlled comparisons, while a complementary acoustic track preserves naturally occurring non-speech evidence. Evidence-grounded generation, shortcut checks, and language-expert review provide auditable questions without translating a shared source set or injecting target sounds. We evaluate ten audio-language models and conduct pooled diagnostics on a fixed eight-model cohort. Language rankings change across domains and tasks; acoustic-semantic performance gaps vary with the requested operation; and temporal errors can persist after the correct event is identified. Long-range retrieval is comparatively strong, while precise clock alignment and factual grounding of natural acoustic events remain fragile. MuLA-Bench thus exposes conditional failure patterns that a single long-context score does not capture.
